summary: # Advanced AD trust-boundary reference Use only within the root skill's explicit confirmation gate. This is a review checklist, not an instruction to extract credentials or deploy persistence. All active testing belongs in an owner-approved synthetic lab. ## Delegation - Unconstrained delegation: inspect effective configuration and whether a delegatable principal actually authenticates to the service. A TGT is not guaranteed for every authentication; account protections and protocol behavior matter. Do not coerce a real controller or collect other users' tickets. - Constrained delegation: inspect allowed service principals, protocol transition and the delegating identity's actual credentials/permissions. A listed target alone does not demonstrate arbitrary impersonation. - Resource-based constrained delegation: inspect who can write the target's delegation descriptor and which principals are allowed. Creating a machine or changing the descriptor is a persistent directory mutation, not reconnaissance. Preserve the original descriptor and use a synthetic account if a lab change is authorized. ## GPO control Trace effective edit/ownership rights, GPO links, filtering, target OU and policy application. A writable GPO can imply significant risk, but actual affected computers/users and resulting privileges must be established. Do not add admin users, immediate tasks or disguised update jobs as a routine proof. Use an inert lab policy marker and verify removal/application afterward. ## RODC Inspect password-replication policy, filtered attribute set, cached/revealed principals and effective rights for the actual configuration. Do not assume all sensitive attributes or all users are automatically excluded or that every RODC key enables unrestricted domain impersonation. RODC key/credential disclosure is incident material; avoid acquiring it for a checklist.
